name: Question 2
problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=3x(t)-2y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=4y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=3,$ for which the corresponding eigenvectors are ${v}_{1}=[2,\text{ }-1]^{T}$ and ${v}_{2}=[1,\text{ }0]^{T},$ respectively. Select the correct options in the reasoning below.The general solution of the system is

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]={c}_{1}\cdot {{field-1}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}\cdot {{field-2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y={{field-3}}
$$

and the straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{1}{e}^{4t}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$
lie on that line.
